LESSON: EYE-HAND COORDINATION SKILLS

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: WRITING
Topic 4.4: Eye-hand coordination skills

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Eye-hand coordination skills. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: when practise folding and tearing along a write?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Take pleasure in participating in eye-hand coordination activities in class. shape outlines and cut out the shapes, sort beads, small stones in a tray and practise picking beads from one tray to another. and drop activities using digital devices. 35 Learners could be involved in pegging puzzles and fitting templates. freely on a computer key board. modeling using clay, dough or plasticine. enhance eye-hand coordination. and printing activities, joining dots, and tracing. small beads or small stones from one person to the other in a left to right direction.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Eye-hand coordination skills.
2. Explain Eye-hand coordination skills to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Eye-hand coordination skills.

5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Eye-hand coordination skills. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: when practise folding and tearing along a write?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
